```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.RAMSimulation.Sim.RunEncoding
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.NondeterministicSpace

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Choice slices of the RAM simulation phases

An instruction's only genuine choice is at its entry. After that first transition the entry
is never reached again, so any remaining choice word follows the corresponding fixed slice.
The forwarding tape embedding lifts the two deterministic slices to the host's tape bank.

## Main definitions

* `WordRAM.Sim.runEmbedND`: the forwarding embedding of a binary-choice phase.

## Main results

* `WordRAM.Sim.runEmbedND_fixChoice`: each slice is the forwarding embedding of its source.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§2.1.2: branches of a nondeterministic machine.)
-/

namespace WordRAM.Sim

open Turing

/-- The nondeterministic forwarding embedding uses the existing deterministic tape embedding
for each choice. It adds no control states or transitions beyond that transformation. -/
@[simps (config := { isSimp := false }) q₀ tr]
def runEmbedND {K : ℕ} {S : Type} (σ : Fin 8 ↪ Fin K) (N : NDTM 8 Bool S) :
    NDTM K Bool S where
  q₀ := N.q₀
  tr b := (embedEmitTM σ (N.fixChoice b)).tr

/-- Fixing a choice in the nondeterministic tape embedding gives exactly the corresponding
deterministic forwarding embedding. -/
theorem runEmbedND_fixChoice {K : ℕ} {S : Type} (σ : Fin 8 ↪ Fin K)
    (N : NDTM 8 Bool S) (b : Bool) :
    (runEmbedND σ N).fixChoice b = embedEmitTM σ (N.fixChoice b) := by
  have hq : ((runEmbedND σ N).fixChoice b).q₀ =
      (embedEmitTM σ (N.fixChoice b)).q₀ := by
    rw [NDTM.fixChoice_q₀, runEmbedND_q₀, embedEmitTM_q₀, NDTM.fixChoice_q₀]
  have ht : ((runEmbedND σ N).fixChoice b).tr =
      (embedEmitTM σ (N.fixChoice b)).tr := by
    funext q inp work
    rw [NDTM.fixChoice_tr, runEmbedND_tr]
  calc (runEmbedND σ N).fixChoice b
      = ⟨((runEmbedND σ N).fixChoice b).q₀, ((runEmbedND σ N).fixChoice b).tr⟩ := rfl
    _ = ⟨(embedEmitTM σ (N.fixChoice b)).q₀, (embedEmitTM σ (N.fixChoice b)).tr⟩ := by
      rw [hq, ht]
    _ = embedEmitTM σ (N.fixChoice b) := rfl

/-- If no transition of a phase enters `entry`, every positive-time configuration of either
deterministic slice avoids that state, from any starting configuration. -/
theorem runSlice_avoids_entry {K : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool}
    (N : NDTM K Bool S) (entry : S)
    (hentry : ∀ (b : Bool) (q : S) inp work, (N.tr b q inp work).state ≠ some entry)
    (b : Bool) (d : Turing.Cfg K Bool S x) (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t) :
    ((N.fixChoice b).runFrom d t).state ≠ some entry := by
  obtain ⟨u, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_succ_of_ne_zero (Nat.ne_of_gt ht)
  rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step']
  cases hs : ((N.fixChoice b).runFrom d u).state with
  | none =>
    rw [MultiTapeTM.step_of_halt hs, hs]
    intro h
    cases h
  | some q =>
    rw [MultiTapeTM.step_of_some hs, Action.apply_state, NDTM.fixChoice_tr]
    exact hentry b q _ _

/-- A phase whose only possible choice is its unrepeated entry follows the slice selected by
the first bit of the branch. All later bits are immaterial.

**Proof sketch.** Take the first step in the chosen slice. Every later live state differs
from the entry by `runSlice_avoids_entry`, so the published deterministic-slice transfer
`Turing.NDTM.runWith_eq_fixChoice_runFrom` applies to the entire tail. -/
theorem runWith_entry_slice {K : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool}
    (N : NDTM K Bool S) (entry : S)
    (hentry : ∀ (b : Bool) (q : S) inp work, (N.tr b q inp work).state ≠ some entry)
    (hagree : ∀ q : S, q ≠ entry → N.tr false q = N.tr true q)
    (b : Bool) (w : List Bool) (d : Turing.Cfg K Bool S x) :
    N.runWith (b :: w) d = (N.fixChoice b).runFrom d (w.length + 1) := by
  rw [NDTM.runWith_cons, NDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step,
    MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step]
  apply NDTM.runWith_eq_fixChoice_runFrom
  intro j _ q hq
  apply hagree
  intro he
  subst q
  apply runSlice_avoids_entry N entry hentry b d (j + 1) (Nat.succ_pos _)
  rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step]
  exact hq

/-- Either slice of the deterministic-to-nondeterministic embedding is the original machine. -/
theorem runDet_fixChoice {K : ℕ} {S : Type} (M : MultiTapeTM K Bool S) (b : Bool) :
    M.toNDTM.fixChoice b = M := by
  have hq : (M.toNDTM.fixChoice b).q₀ = M.q₀ := by
    rw [NDTM.fixChoice_q₀, MultiTapeTM.toNDTM_q₀]
  have ht : (M.toNDTM.fixChoice b).tr = M.tr := by
    funext q inp work
    rw [NDTM.fixChoice_tr, MultiTapeTM.toNDTM_tr]
  calc M.toNDTM.fixChoice b
      = ⟨(M.toNDTM.fixChoice b).q₀, (M.toNDTM.fixChoice b).tr⟩ := rfl
    _ = ⟨M.q₀, M.tr⟩ := by rw [hq, ht]
    _ = M := rfl

/-- The forwarding nondeterministic embedding commutes with every branch, preserving the
ambient frame and forwarding the source output.

**Proof sketch.** Induct on the choice word. One step under its head bit is a step of the
corresponding deterministic embedding, by `runEmbedND_fixChoice`, and the existing one-step
case of `Turing.embedEmitTM_runFrom` transports that step. -/
theorem runEmbedND_runWith {K : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool}
    (σ : Fin 8 ↪ Fin K) (N : NDTM 8 Bool S)
    (tapes : Fin K → ℤ → Option Bool) (heads : Fin K → ℤ) (pre : List Bool)
    (w : List Bool) (d : Turing.Cfg 8 Bool S x) :
    (runEmbedND σ N).runWith w (embedEmitCfg σ tapes heads pre d) =
      embedEmitCfg σ tapes heads pre (N.runWith w d) := by
  induction w generalizing d with
  | nil => rw [NDTM.runWith_nil, NDTM.runWith_nil]
  | cons b w ih =>
    rw [NDTM.runWith_cons, NDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step, runEmbedND_fixChoice,
      ← MultiTapeTM.runFrom_one, embedEmitTM_runFrom, MultiTapeTM.runFrom_one,
      ← NDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step, ih, NDTM.runWith_cons]

/-- A constant choice word follows the corresponding fixed slice, even when the machine's
two transitions differ. This also covers the empty word. -/
theorem runWith_replicate {K : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool}
    (N : NDTM K Bool S) (b : Bool) (t : ℕ) (d : Turing.Cfg K Bool S x) :
    N.runWith (List.replicate t b) d = (N.fixChoice b).runFrom d t := by
  induction t generalizing d with
  | zero => rw [List.replicate_zero, NDTM.runWith_nil, MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero]
  | succ t ih =>
    rw [List.replicate_succ, NDTM.runWith_cons, NDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step, ih,
      MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step]

end WordRAM.Sim
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/RAMSimulation/Sim/RunSource.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.RAMSimulation.Sim.Phases
import Mathlib.Data.List.GetD

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Source-run facts for the RAM simulation

These facts read extended RAM steps through `WordRAM.xstep_def` and the run readers. They
connect instruction fetch, coin consumption and the exact footprint to the host induction.

## Main definitions

No new source-machine operation is defined here.

## Main results

* `WordRAM.Sim.source_pc_lt`: a non-verdict step is at a position inside the program.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (Exercise 1.9; §2.1.2.)
-/

namespace WordRAM.Sim

/-- A step that continues instead of giving a verdict must fetch inside the program;
the default instruction past the end rejects. -/
theorem source_pc_lt {W : ℕ} {P : XProgram} {x ρ : List Bool} {c c' : XCfg W}
    (h : xstep P x ρ c = .inl c') : c.pc < P.length := by
  by_contra hp
  rw [xstep_def, List.getD_eq_default P (.base .reject) (Nat.le_of_not_gt hp)] at h
  cases h

/-- A source step depends on a stream only through the bit at its current coin counter, and
only when the fetched instruction is a coin. -/
theorem source_step_coin_congr {W : ℕ} (P : XProgram) (x ρ τ : List Bool) (c : XCfg W)
    (hbits : isCoin (P.getD c.pc (.base .reject)) = true →
      ρ.getD c.rd false = τ.getD c.rd false) :
    xstep P x ρ c = xstep P x τ c := by
  rw [xstep_def, xstep_def]
  cases hf : P.getD c.pc (.base .reject) with
  | base i => cases i <;> rfl
  | rdIn i j => rfl
  | emit i => rfl
  | coin i => rw [hbits (by rw [hf, isCoin_def])]
  | half i j => rfl

/-- A stream agrees with a finite consumed coin prefix at every index already present in
that prefix. The stream may be shorter if its default false bits give the same values. -/
def RunCoinsAgree (coins ρ : List Bool) : Prop :=
  ∀ i < coins.length, coins.getD i false = ρ.getD i false

/-- Agreement of consumed coins means equality of their defaulted reads at every consumed
index. This is the defining equivalence of `RunCoinsAgree`. -/
theorem runCoinsAgree_iff (coins ρ : List Bool) :
    RunCoinsAgree coins ρ ↔ ∀ i < coins.length, coins.getD i false = ρ.getD i false := Iff.rfl

/-- Every finite coin prefix agrees with itself. -/
theorem runCoinsAgree_refl (coins : List Bool) : RunCoinsAgree coins coins := fun _ _ => rfl

/-- Agreement with an extended consumed prefix implies agreement with the earlier prefix. -/
theorem runCoinsAgree_append_left (coins extra ρ : List Bool)
    (h : RunCoinsAgree (coins ++ extra) ρ) : RunCoinsAgree coins ρ := by
  rw [runCoinsAgree_iff] at h ⊢
  intro i hi
  have h' := h i (by rw [List.length_append]; omega)
  rw [List.getD_append coins extra false i hi] at h'
  exact h'

/-- An exact non-verdict source trace records precisely the union of the cells touched by
its instructions, rather than an arbitrary enclosing footprint. This internal relation lets
the branch induction compare its accumulated table cells with a `HaltsWithin` witness. -/
inductive RunSourceTrace {W : ℕ} (P : XProgram) (x ρ : List Bool) :
    ℕ → XCfg W → XCfg W → Finset ℤ → Prop
  | nil (c : XCfg W) : RunSourceTrace P x ρ 0 c c ∅
  | cons {n : ℕ} {c c₁ c' : XCfg W} {K : Finset ℤ}
      (step : xstep P x ρ c = .inl c₁) (tail : RunSourceTrace P x ρ n c₁ c' K) :
      RunSourceTrace P x ρ (n + 1) c c' ((P.getD c.pc (.base .reject)).touches c.mem ∪ K)

/-- An exact source trace is a footprint run inside any set containing its touched cells.

**Proof sketch.** Induct on the exact trace. Each constructor records the current instruction's
touch set unioned with the tail's cells, so the enclosing-set hypothesis supplies both the
current footprint clause and the tail induction hypothesis in `XStepsIn.succ_iff`. -/
theorem RunSourceTrace.to_stepsIn {W : ℕ} {P : XProgram} {x ρ : List Bool}
    {n : ℕ} {c c' : XCfg W} {K : Finset ℤ} (h : RunSourceTrace P x ρ n c c' K)
    (L : Set ℤ) (hK : ∀ z ∈ K, z ∈ L) : XStepsIn P x ρ L n c c' := by
  induction h generalizing L with
  | nil c => exact XStepsIn.zero_iff.mpr rfl
  | cons hs ht ih =>
    apply XStepsIn.succ_iff.mpr
    refine ⟨_, hs, ?_, ih L ?_⟩
    · intro z hz
      exact hK z (Finset.mem_union.mpr (Or.inl hz))
    · intro z hz
      exact hK z (Finset.mem_union.mpr (Or.inr hz))

/-- An exact non-verdict prefix of a run that eventually halts has no more steps than the
halting run, and all of its touched cells belong to the halting run's footprint.

**Proof sketch.** Compare the exact trace with the `XStepsIn` witness one step at a time.
If the halting witness has zero remaining ordinary steps, a further exact step contradicts
its verdict. Otherwise determinism identifies the first successor, the footprint clause
bounds this step's cells, and the induction hypothesis bounds the remaining prefix. This is
the prefix/footprint comparison; completed verdicts are compared with `HaltsWithin.unique`. -/
theorem RunSourceTrace.bounded_by_halt {W : ℕ} {P : XProgram} {x ρ : List Bool}
    {n : ℕ} {c c' : XCfg W} {K : Finset ℤ} (h : RunSourceTrace P x ρ n c c' K)
    {L : Set ℤ} {m : ℕ} {c₂ : XCfg W} {v : Bool}
    (hr : XStepsIn P x ρ L m c c₂) (hv : xstep P x ρ c₂ = .inr v) :
    n ≤ m ∧ ∀ z ∈ K, z ∈ L := by
  induction h generalizing m c₂ with
  | nil c =>
    refine ⟨Nat.zero_le _, ?_⟩
    intro z hz
    exact (Finset.notMem_empty z hz).elim
  | cons hs ht ih =>
    cases m with
    | zero =>
      have heq := XStepsIn.zero_iff.mp hr
      subst c₂
      have hbad := hs.symm.trans hv
      cases hbad
    | succ m =>
      obtain ⟨d, hd, hcells, htail⟩ := XStepsIn.succ_iff.mp hr
      have heq := Sum.inl.inj (hs.symm.trans hd)
      subst d
      obtain ⟨hn, hK⟩ := ih htail hv
      refine ⟨Nat.succ_le_succ hn, ?_⟩
      intro z hz
      rcases Finset.mem_union.mp hz with hz | hz
      · exact hcells hz
      · exact hK z hz

/-- Agreement with a consumed prefix ending in `b` makes the stream's read at that newly
consumed index equal to `b`, including when the earlier prefix is empty. -/
theorem runCoinsAgree_append_bit (coins ρ : List Bool) (b : Bool)
    (h : RunCoinsAgree (coins ++ [b]) ρ) : ρ.getD coins.length false = b := by
  rw [runCoinsAgree_iff] at h
  have h' := h coins.length (by rw [List.length_append, List.length_singleton]; omega)
  rw [List.getD_append_right coins [b] false coins.length le_rfl, Nat.sub_self] at h'
  change b = ρ.getD coins.length false at h'
  exact h'.symm

/-- A continuing source step increments the coin counter exactly for a coin instruction. -/
theorem source_step_rd {W : ℕ} {P : XProgram} {x ρ : List Bool} {c c' : XCfg W}
    (h : xstep P x ρ c = .inl c') :
    c'.rd = c.rd + (if isCoin (P.getD c.pc (.base .reject)) then 1 else 0) := by
  rw [xstep_def] at h
  split at h <;> cases h <;>
    simp_all only [isCoin_def, reduceCtorEq, if_true, if_false, Nat.add_zero]

/-- An instruction giving a verdict is not a coin, so it consumes no stream bit. -/
theorem source_verdict_not_coin {W : ℕ} {P : XProgram} {x ρ : List Bool}
    {c : XCfg W} {v : Bool} (h : xstep P x ρ c = .inr v) :
    isCoin (P.getD c.pc (.base .reject)) = false := by
  rw [xstep_def] at h
  split at h <;> cases h <;> simp_all only [isCoin_def]

/-- A source verdict remains the same under any replacement of the coin stream. -/
theorem source_verdict_stream {W : ℕ} {P : XProgram} {x ρ : List Bool}
    {c : XCfg W} {v : Bool} (h : xstep P x ρ c = .inr v) (τ : List Bool) :
    xstep P x τ c = .inr v := by
  apply (source_step_coin_congr P x τ ρ c ?_).trans h
  intro hc
  rw [source_verdict_not_coin h] at hc
  cases hc

/-- Every consumed coin in a prefix satisfies the indicated predicate at its index. -/
def RunCoinsSatisfy (B : ℕ → Bool → Prop) (coins : List Bool) : Prop :=
  ∀ i < coins.length, B i (coins.getD i false)

/-- A prefix satisfies its indexed coin predicate exactly at its consumed indices. -/
theorem runCoinsSatisfy_iff (B : ℕ → Bool → Prop) (coins : List Bool) :
    RunCoinsSatisfy B coins ↔ ∀ i < coins.length, B i (coins.getD i false) := Iff.rfl

/-- The empty consumed prefix satisfies every indexed coin predicate. -/
theorem runCoinsSatisfy_nil (B : ℕ → Bool → Prop) : RunCoinsSatisfy B [] :=
  fun i hi => (Nat.not_lt_zero i hi).elim

/-- Appending a permitted bit at the next coin index preserves the indexed coin predicate. -/
theorem runCoinsSatisfy_append (B : ℕ → Bool → Prop) (coins : List Bool) (b : Bool)
    (h : RunCoinsSatisfy B coins) (hb : B coins.length b) : RunCoinsSatisfy B (coins ++ [b]) := by
  rw [runCoinsSatisfy_iff] at h ⊢
  intro i hi
  by_cases hip : i < coins.length
  · rw [List.getD_append coins [b] false i hip]
    exact h i hip
  · have hie : i = coins.length := by rw [List.length_append, List.length_singleton] at hi; omega
    subst i
    rw [List.getD_append_right coins [b] false coins.length le_rfl, Nat.sub_self]
    change B coins.length b
    exact hb

/-- The consumed coin prefix after one instruction: append its entry bit for a coin, and
keep the prefix for every other instruction. -/
def runNextCoins (ins : XInstr) (coins : List Bool) (b : Bool) : List Bool :=
  if isCoin ins then coins ++ [b] else coins

/-- The next consumed prefix is given by the instruction's coin test. -/
theorem runNextCoins_eq (ins : XInstr) (coins : List Bool) (b : Bool) :
    runNextCoins ins coins b = if isCoin ins then coins ++ [b] else coins := rfl

/-- A consumed prefix grows by exactly one bit for a coin and by zero otherwise. -/
theorem runNextCoins_length (ins : XInstr) (coins : List Bool) (b : Bool) :
    (runNextCoins ins coins b).length = coins.length + (if isCoin ins then 1 else 0) := by
  cases hc : isCoin ins <;>
    simp only [runNextCoins_eq, hc, reduceCtorEq, if_true, if_false,
      List.length_append, List.length_singleton, Nat.add_zero]

/-- The next consumed prefix extends the current one, by either an empty suffix or one bit. -/
theorem runNextCoins_prefix (ins : XInstr) (coins : List Bool) (b : Bool) :
    ∃ extra, runNextCoins ins coins b = coins ++ extra := by
  cases hc : isCoin ins with
  | false =>
    refine ⟨[], ?_⟩
    simp only [runNextCoins_eq, hc, reduceCtorEq, if_false, List.append_nil]
  | true =>
    refine ⟨[b], ?_⟩
    simp only [runNextCoins_eq, hc, if_true]

/-- A stream agreeing with the next consumed prefix supplies the selected entry bit whenever
the instruction is a coin. -/
theorem runNextCoins_read (ins : XInstr) (coins ρ : List Bool) (b : Bool)
    (h : RunCoinsAgree (runNextCoins ins coins b) ρ) :
    isCoin ins = true → ρ.getD coins.length false = b := by
  intro hc
  apply runCoinsAgree_append_bit coins ρ b
  simpa only [runNextCoins_eq, hc, reduceCtorEq, if_true] using h

/-- Updating the consumed prefix preserves its indexed predicate when the selected next bit
is permitted. Non-coin instructions leave that prefix unchanged. -/
theorem runNextCoins_satisfy (B : ℕ → Bool → Prop) (ins : XInstr) (coins : List Bool) (b : Bool)
    (h : RunCoinsSatisfy B coins) (hb : B coins.length b) :
    RunCoinsSatisfy B (runNextCoins ins coins b) := by
  cases hc : isCoin ins with
  | false => simpa only [runNextCoins_eq, hc, reduceCtorEq, if_false] using h
  | true => simpa only [runNextCoins_eq, hc, reduceCtorEq, if_true] using
      runCoinsSatisfy_append B coins b h hb

end WordRAM.Sim
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/RAMSimulation/Sim/RunSpace.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.RAMSimulation.Sim.RunSlices

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Visited-cell bounds for the RAM host

The start-up's visited cells are counted once. Subsequent instruction phases use fixed
head origins, so their union is bounded by one interval per tape, independently of the
number of instructions. These lemmas read the deterministic and nondeterministic space
measures through their published equations.

## Main definitions

No new space measure is introduced.

## Main results

* `WordRAM.Sim.runSpace_eq_of_clamped_heads`: a branch with a clamped deterministic head
  trajectory visits exactly the deterministic run's cells.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (Definition 4.1: visited work-tape cells.)
-/

namespace WordRAM.Sim

open Turing

/-- A branch whose head positions follow a deterministic run through time `t`, then repeat
its last positions, uses exactly that run's space, provided the branch is at least `t` long.

**Proof sketch.** On each tape a visited branch position at time `u` is the source position at
`min u t`. Conversely each source time at most `t` is a valid branch prefix and is fixed by
that minimum. The two visited sets agree; take their cardinalities and sum over tapes. -/
theorem runSpace_eq_of_clamped_heads {K : ℕ} {S H : Type} {x : List Bool}
    (N : NDTM K Bool S) (M : MultiTapeTM K Bool H)
    (w : List Bool) (d : Turing.Cfg K Bool S x) (e : Turing.Cfg K Bool H x) (t : ℕ)
    (ht : t ≤ w.length)
    (hheads : ∀ u ≤ w.length, ∀ j,
      (N.runWith (w.take u) d).workTapePos j = (M.runFrom e (min u t)).workTapePos j) :
    N.spaceUsedWith w d = M.spaceUsed e t := by
  have hvisited : ∀ j, N.visitedWith w d j = M.visitedByTapeHead e t j := by
    intro j
    apply Finset.ext
    intro z
    rw [NDTM.visitedWith_eq, M.mem_visitedByTapeHead_iff]
    constructor
    · intro hz
      obtain ⟨u, hu, hpos⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hz
      have hul : u ≤ w.length := Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp (Finset.mem_range.mp hu)
      refine ⟨min u t, min_le_right _ _, ?_⟩
      rw [← hheads u hul j]
      exact hpos
    · rintro ⟨u, hu, hpos⟩
      refine Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨u, Finset.mem_range.mpr (Nat.lt_succ_iff.mpr (hu.trans ht)), ?_⟩
      rw [hheads u (hu.trans ht) j, min_eq_left hu]
      exact hpos
  rw [NDTM.spaceUsedWith_eq, M.spaceUsed_eq_sum]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro j hj
  rw [M.spaceUsedByTape_eq_card, hvisited j]

/-- The space along a constant choice word is exactly the deterministic slice's space.
No agreement between the machine's two transition functions is required. -/
theorem runSpace_replicate {K : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool}
    (N : NDTM K Bool S) (b : Bool) (t : ℕ) (d : Turing.Cfg K Bool S x) :
    N.spaceUsedWith (List.replicate t b) d = (N.fixChoice b).spaceUsed d t := by
  apply runSpace_eq_of_clamped_heads
  · rw [List.length_replicate]
  · intro u hu j
    rw [List.take_replicate, runWith_replicate]

/-- Two branch segments with the same head envelope retain that envelope after concatenation
when the first segment restores the starting head vector. Radii therefore do not accumulate
over successive RAM instructions. -/
theorem runEnvelope_append {K : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool}
    (N : NDTM K Bool S) (w₀ w₁ : List Bool) (d e : Turing.Cfg K Bool S x) (R : ℕ)
    (hr : N.runWith w₀ d = e) (hh : e.workTapePos = d.workTapePos)
    (h₀ : ∀ u ≤ w₀.length, ∀ j,
      |(N.runWith (w₀.take u) d).workTapePos j - d.workTapePos j| ≤ (R : ℤ))
    (h₁ : ∀ u ≤ w₁.length, ∀ j,
      |(N.runWith (w₁.take u) e).workTapePos j - e.workTapePos j| ≤ (R : ℤ)) :
    ∀ u ≤ (w₀ ++ w₁).length, ∀ j,
      |(N.runWith ((w₀ ++ w₁).take u) d).workTapePos j - d.workTapePos j| ≤ (R : ℤ) := by
  intro u hu j
  by_cases hu₀ : u ≤ w₀.length
  · rw [List.take_append_of_le_length hu₀]
    exact h₀ u hu₀ j
  · have hu₁ : u - w₀.length ≤ w₁.length := by rw [List.length_append] at hu; omega
    rw [List.take_append, List.take_of_length_le (by omega), NDTM.runWith_append, hr]
    simpa only [hh] using h₁ (u - w₀.length) hu₁ j

/-- Appending a branch whose heads remain in radius `R` adds at most `K·(2R+1)` visited
cells to the first segment's space. The first segment's space occurs with coefficient one.

**Proof sketch.** Split each visited prefix before or after the first word. Its head belongs
either to the first segment's visited set or to the second segment's interval about its
starting head. Bound the union's cardinality by the sum of cardinalities; `Int.card_Icc`
counts the interval. Sum the resulting inequality over the `K` tapes. -/
theorem runSpace_append_le {K : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool}
    (N : NDTM K Bool S) (w₀ w₁ : List Bool) (d e : Turing.Cfg K Bool S x) (R : ℕ)
    (hr : N.runWith w₀ d = e)
    (henv : ∀ u ≤ w₁.length, ∀ j,
      |(N.runWith (w₁.take u) e).workTapePos j - e.workTapePos j| ≤ (R : ℤ)) :
    N.spaceUsedWith (w₀ ++ w₁) d ≤ N.spaceUsedWith w₀ d + K * (2 * R + 1) := by
  have hone : ∀ j, (N.visitedWith (w₀ ++ w₁) d j).card ≤
      (N.visitedWith w₀ d j).card + (2 * R + 1) := by
    intro j
    let I := Finset.Icc (e.workTapePos j - (R : ℤ)) (e.workTapePos j + (R : ℤ))
    have hsub : N.visitedWith (w₀ ++ w₁) d j ⊆ N.visitedWith w₀ d j ∪ I := by
      intro z hz
      rw [NDTM.visitedWith_eq] at hz
      obtain ⟨u, hu, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hz
      have hul : u ≤ (w₀ ++ w₁).length := Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp (Finset.mem_range.mp hu)
      by_cases hfirst : u ≤ w₀.length
      · apply Finset.mem_union.mpr; left
        rw [NDTM.visitedWith_eq, List.take_append_of_le_length hfirst]
        exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨u, Finset.mem_range.mpr (Nat.lt_succ_iff.mpr hfirst), rfl⟩
      · apply Finset.mem_union.mpr; right
        have htail : u - w₀.length ≤ w₁.length := by rw [List.length_append] at hul; omega
        rw [List.take_append, List.take_of_length_le (by omega), NDTM.runWith_append, hr]
        exact Finset.mem_Icc.mpr (by
          obtain ⟨hlo, hhi⟩ := abs_le.mp (henv (u - w₀.length) htail j)
          constructor <;> omega)
    have hcard : I.card = 2 * R + 1 := by
      rw [Int.card_Icc]
      have heq : e.workTapePos j + (R : ℤ) + 1 - (e.workTapePos j - (R : ℤ)) =
          ((2 * R + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) := by push_cast; ring
      rw [heq, Int.toNat_natCast]
    exact (Finset.card_le_card hsub).trans ((Finset.card_union_le _ _).trans (by rw [hcard]))
  rw [NDTM.spaceUsedWith_eq, NDTM.spaceUsedWith_eq]
  calc
    _ ≤ ∑ j : Fin K, ((N.visitedWith w₀ d j).card + (2 * R + 1)) :=
      Finset.sum_le_sum (fun j _ => hone j)
    _ = _ := by simp only [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ,
      Fintype.card_fin, smul_eq_mul, Nat.mul_add]

end WordRAM.Sim
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/RAMSimulation/Sim/RunStartup.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.RAMSimulation.Sim.RunStep
import TCSlib.Complexity.RAMSimulation.Sim.RunSpace

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Start-up inside the finite simulation host

The start-up runs deterministically under every choice word and takes one stationary dispatch
step into the first RAM instruction. That extra step visits no new work-tape cells, preserving
the leading time and space costs of the word-size witness.

## Main definitions

No additional machine is constructed here.

## Main results

* `WordRAM.Sim.RunSetup.host_initCfg`: the host's initial configuration is the tagged
  start-up entry configuration.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (Exercise 1.9; Definition 4.1.)
-/

namespace WordRAM.Sim.RunSetup

open Turing

variable {P : XProgram} {fn : Bool} {Mw : FinTM Bool} (A : RunSetup P fn Mw)

/-- The host starts with the start-up entry tagged by the initial phase; its tapes, heads,
input position and output are exactly the corresponding initial configuration's fields. -/
theorem host_initCfg (x : List Bool) :
    (Turing.Cfg.init A.startEntry x).mapState (fun q => (⟨none, q⟩ : A.State)) =
      A.host.initCfg x := by
  rw [NDTM.initCfg_eq, host_q₀]
  apply Cfg.mapState_eq_of_fields
  · rw [Cfg.init_state, Cfg.init_state, Option.map_some]
  · rw [Cfg.init_inputPos, Cfg.init_inputPos]
  · funext j p
    rw [Cfg.init_workTapes, Cfg.init_workTapes]
  · funext j
    rw [Cfg.init_workTapePos, Cfg.init_workTapePos]
  · rw [Cfg.init_output, Cfg.init_output]

/-- Any choice word for the start-up, followed by one arbitrary dispatch bit, reaches the
first instruction with the initial RAM encoding. The host's prefix heads are exactly the
start-up heads, and the dispatch endpoint repeats their final positions.

**Proof sketch.** Use `start_correct` for the chosen start-up time and origins. Its phase is
deterministic, so `MultiTapeTM.toNDTM_runWith` identifies every word prefix with that run.
The no-earlier-exit clause supplies the host guard, and `host_phase_dispatch` performs the
one stationary redirect. Encoding and head positions are preserved by its state tag. -/
theorem startup_trajectory (x : List Bool) (W tw sw : ℕ)
    (hW : Mw.ComputesInTime x (Nat.bits W) tw)
    (hS : Mw.tm.spaceUsed (Mw.tm.initCfg x) tw ≤ sw)
    (words : ℕ → List Bool) (hlen : ∀ n, (words n).length = n) (dispatch : ℕ → Bool) :
    ∃ (t : ℕ) (o : Fin 8 → ℤ) (d' : Turing.Cfg (8 + A.extraTapes) Bool A.State x),
      t ≤ tw + A.startCost * (x.length + W ^ 2 + 1) ∧
      A.host.runWith (words t ++ [dispatch t]) (A.host.initCfg x) = d' ∧
      d'.state = some ⟨some (0, false), (A.phases 0).entry⟩ ∧
      Encodes A.width fn {-1} (XCfg.init W x.length) (Fin.castAddEmb A.extraTapes) o d' ∧
      (∀ u ≤ t, ∀ j,
        (A.host.runWith ((words t).take u) (A.host.initCfg x)).workTapePos j =
          (A.startup.runFrom (Turing.Cfg.init A.startEntry x) u).workTapePos j) ∧
      d'.workTapePos = (A.startup.runFrom (Turing.Cfg.init A.startEntry x) t).workTapePos ∧
      A.startup.spaceUsed (Turing.Cfg.init A.startEntry x) t ≤
        sw + A.startCost * (W + (Nat.bits x.length).length + 1) := by
  obtain ⟨t, o, ht, hcut, hexit, he, hspace⟩ := A.start_correct x W tw sw hW hS
  let d₀ : Turing.Cfg (8 + A.extraTapes) Bool A.StartState x := Turing.Cfg.init A.startEntry x
  let e := A.startup.runFrom d₀ t
  let w := words t
  have hw : w.length = t := hlen t
  have hr : (A.phase none).runWith w d₀ = e := by
    rw [phase_none, MultiTapeTM.toNDTM_runWith, hw]
  let q₀ : A.State := ⟨some (0, false), (A.phases 0).entry⟩
  have hred : A.redirect none A.startExit = some q₀ := by
    rw [redirect_none, if_pos rfl]
  have hg : ∀ u < w.length, ∀ q, ((A.phase none).runWith (w.take u) d₀).state = some q →
      A.redirect none q = none := by
    intro u hu q hq
    rw [phase_none, MultiTapeTM.toNDTM_runWith, List.length_take_of_le hu.le] at hq
    have hneq : q ≠ A.startExit := by
      intro heq
      apply hcut u (by omega)
      exact hq.trans (congrArg some heq)
    rw [redirect_none, if_neg hneq]
  obtain ⟨hpre, hfinal⟩ := A.host_phase_dispatch none d₀ e w hr A.startExit hexit q₀ hred hg
    (dispatch t)
  rw [host_initCfg] at hpre hfinal
  refine ⟨t, o, e.mapState (fun _ => q₀), ht, hfinal, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, hspace⟩
  · rw [Cfg.mapState_state, hexit, Option.map_some]
  · exact (encodes_mapState A.width fn {-1} (XCfg.init W x.length)
      (Fin.castAddEmb A.extraTapes) o e (fun _ => q₀)).mp he
  · intro u hu j
    have huw : u ≤ w.length := by omega
    rw [hpre u huw, Cfg.mapState_workTapePos, phase_none,
      MultiTapeTM.toNDTM_runWith, List.length_take_of_le huw]
  · funext j
    rw [Cfg.mapState_workTapePos]

/-- Start-up and its dispatch enter the initial RAM encoding with the original additive
startup space bound. The dispatch visits no cell not already visited by the start-up.

**Proof sketch.** Use `startup_trajectory`. Through time `t` the host heads are the start-up
heads; the extra dispatch step repeats the time-`t` positions. Thus
`runSpace_eq_of_clamped_heads` identifies their visited sets exactly, preserving the leading
`sw` term rather than multiplying it by a constant. -/
theorem startup_run (x : List Bool) (W tw sw : ℕ)
    (hW : Mw.ComputesInTime x (Nat.bits W) tw)
    (hS : Mw.tm.spaceUsed (Mw.tm.initCfg x) tw ≤ sw)
    (words : ℕ → List Bool) (hlen : ∀ n, (words n).length = n) (dispatch : ℕ → Bool) :
    ∃ (t : ℕ) (o : Fin 8 → ℤ) (d' : Turing.Cfg (8 + A.extraTapes) Bool A.State x),
      t ≤ tw + A.startCost * (x.length + W ^ 2 + 1) ∧
      A.host.runWith (words t ++ [dispatch t]) (A.host.initCfg x) = d' ∧
      d'.state = some ⟨some (0, false), (A.phases 0).entry⟩ ∧
      Encodes A.width fn {-1} (XCfg.init W x.length) (Fin.castAddEmb A.extraTapes) o d' ∧
      A.host.spaceUsedWith (words t ++ [dispatch t]) (A.host.initCfg x) ≤
        sw + A.startCost * (W + (Nat.bits x.length).length + 1) := by
  obtain ⟨t, o, d', ht, hr, hd, he, hprefix, hheads, hs⟩ :=
    A.startup_trajectory x W tw sw hW hS words hlen dispatch
  have hlen' : (words t ++ [dispatch t]).length = t + 1 := by
    rw [List.length_append, hlen t, List.length_singleton]
  have hspace : A.host.spaceUsedWith (words t ++ [dispatch t]) (A.host.initCfg x) =
      A.startup.spaceUsed (Turing.Cfg.init A.startEntry x) t := by
    apply runSpace_eq_of_clamped_heads
    · rw [hlen']
      exact Nat.le_succ _
    · intro u hu j
      by_cases hut : u ≤ t
      · have huw : u ≤ (words t).length := by rw [hlen]; exact hut
        rw [List.take_append_of_le_length huw, hprefix u hut j, min_eq_left hut]
      · have hue : u = t + 1 := by rw [hlen'] at hu; omega
        have hwhole : (words t ++ [dispatch t]).length ≤ u := by rw [hlen', hue]
        rw [List.take_of_length_le hwhole, hr, hheads, min_eq_right (by omega)]
  exact ⟨t, o, d', ht, hr, hd, he, hspace.trans_le hs⟩

end WordRAM.Sim.RunSetup
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/RAMSimulation/Sim/RunStep.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.RAMSimulation.Sim.RunHost
import TCSlib.Complexity.RAMSimulation.Sim.RunSource

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Instruction steps inside the finite simulation host

The host follows one phase until its first redirect, then takes one stationary dispatch step.
The run lemmas here cite the standard phase host and the forwarding tape embedding.

## Main definitions

No additional machine is constructed in this file.

## Main results

* `WordRAM.Sim.RunSetup.host_phase_run`: an unredirected phase branch inside the host.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (Exercise 1.9; §2.1.2.)
-/

namespace WordRAM.Sim.RunSetup

open Turing

variable {P : XProgram} {fn : Bool} {Mw : FinTM Bool} (A : RunSetup P fn Mw)

/-- A branch that encounters no redirect before its end is the corresponding tagged phase
branch, including a last phase that halts at its endpoint.

**Proof sketch.** At an unredirected state, each slice of the host takes the tagged phase
action, by `host_fixChoice` and the published transition equation of `phaseHostTM`.
`Turing.NDTM.runWith_mapState_of_agreeOn` transfers the branch along the phase-state tag. -/
theorem host_phase_run (i : Index (P := P)) {x : List Bool}
    (d : Turing.Cfg (8 + A.extraTapes) Bool (A.PhaseState i) x) (w : List Bool)
    (hguard : ∀ u < w.length, ∀ q, ((A.phase i).runWith (w.take u) d).state = some q →
      A.redirect i q = none) :
    A.host.runWith w (d.mapState (Sigma.mk i)) =
      ((A.phase i).runWith w d).mapState (Sigma.mk i) := by
  apply NDTM.runWith_mapState_of_agreeOn (A.phase i) A.host
    ⟨Sigma.mk i, sigma_mk_injective⟩ (fun q => A.redirect i q = none)
  · intro b q hq inp work
    change A.host.tr b ⟨i, q⟩ inp work =
      ((A.phase i).tr b q inp work).mapState (Sigma.mk i)
    rw [← NDTM.fixChoice_tr (tm := A.host) (b := b), host_fixChoice,
      phaseHostTM_tr_of_red_none _ _ _ i q hq, NDTM.fixChoice_tr]
  · exact hguard

/-- After an unredirected phase branch reaches a redirected live exit, either next choice
performs the stationary dispatch. All shorter prefixes are the tagged phase prefixes. -/
theorem host_phase_dispatch (i : Index (P := P)) {x : List Bool}
    (d d' : Turing.Cfg (8 + A.extraTapes) Bool (A.PhaseState i) x)
    (w : List Bool) (hrun : (A.phase i).runWith w d = d')
    (q : A.PhaseState i) (hs : d'.state = some q) (q' : A.State)
    (hred : A.redirect i q = some q')
    (hguard : ∀ u < w.length, ∀ q, ((A.phase i).runWith (w.take u) d).state = some q →
      A.redirect i q = none) (b : Bool) :
    (∀ u ≤ w.length, A.host.runWith (w.take u) (d.mapState (Sigma.mk i)) =
      ((A.phase i).runWith (w.take u) d).mapState (Sigma.mk i)) ∧
    A.host.runWith (w ++ [b]) (d.mapState (Sigma.mk i)) = d'.mapState (fun _ => q') := by
  simpa only [host_runWith] using
    NDTM.phaseHostND_run A.phase ⟨none, A.startEntry⟩ A.redirect i d d' w hrun q hs q'
      hred hguard b

/-- The redirect selected by an ordinary RAM step enters the phase of the successor program
position and flips parity. A continuing step is inside the program, so its clamped current
position equals its actual program counter. -/
theorem resumeTag_of_step {x ρ : List Bool} {W : ℕ} {c c' : XCfg W}
    (par jump : Bool) (hstep : xstep P x ρ c = .inl c')
    (hpc : c'.pc = if jump then jumpTarget
      (P.getD (runPosition P c.pc).val (.base .reject)) else c.pc + 1) :
    A.resumeTag (runPosition P c.pc) par jump =
      ⟨some (runPosition P c'.pc, !par), (A.phases (runPosition P c'.pc)).entry⟩ := by
  have hp : (runPosition P c.pc).val = c.pc := by
    rw [runPosition_val, min_eq_left (source_pc_lt hstep).le]
  have htarget : (if jump then jumpTarget (P.getD (runPosition P c.pc).val (.base .reject))
      else (runPosition P c.pc).val + 1) = c'.pc := by
    simpa only [hp] using hpc.symm
  rw [resumeTag_eq]
  dsimp only
  rw [htarget]

/-- An instruction's fixed slice has the same endpoint and head envelope after embedding
on the first eight tapes. Every unselected tape head remains at its ambient starting point.

**Proof sketch.** Select the entry bank with `runBank`, apply the chosen phase's correctness
field, and reconstruct the ambient start by `runBank_embed`. The forwarding embedding's run,
selected-head, state, output and frame equations transfer every clause. The resulting
encoding is `encodes_embed`, and the two live exit tags are mapped by `redirect_some`. -/
theorem phase_correct (p : Fin (P.length + 1)) (par b : Bool) {x : List Bool} {W : ℕ}
    (ρ : List Bool) (T : Finset ℤ) (c : XCfg W) (o : Fin 8 → ℤ)
    (d : Turing.Cfg (8 + A.extraTapes) Bool (A.PhaseState (some (p, par))) x)
    (hfetch : P.getD c.pc (.base .reject) = P.getD p.val (.base .reject))
    (hcoin : isCoin (P.getD p.val (.base .reject)) = true → ρ.getD c.rd false = b)
    (hd : d.state = some (A.phases p).entry)
    (he : Encodes A.width fn T c (Fin.castAddEmb A.extraTapes) o d) :
    ∃ (t : ℕ) (d' : Turing.Cfg (8 + A.extraTapes) Bool (A.PhaseState (some (p, par))) x),
      t ≤ (A.phases p).cost * ((T.card + 1) * (W + 1) + W ^ 2 + x.length + 1) ∧
      (∀ u < t, ∀ q, (((A.phase (some (p, par))).fixChoice b).runFrom d u).state = some q →
        A.redirect (some (p, par)) q = none) ∧
      (∀ u ≤ t, ∀ j : Fin 8,
        |(((A.phase (some (p, par))).fixChoice b).runFrom d u).workTapePos
            ((Fin.castAddEmb A.extraTapes) j) - o j| ≤
          ((A.phases p).cost * ((T.card + 1) * (W + 1) + (Nat.bits x.length).length + 1) : ℕ)) ∧
      (∀ u ≤ t, ∀ j : Fin (8 + A.extraTapes), j ∉ Set.range (Fin.castAddEmb A.extraTapes) →
        (((A.phase (some (p, par))).fixChoice b).runFrom d u).workTapePos j = d.workTapePos j) ∧
      ((A.phase (some (p, par))).fixChoice b).runFrom d t = d' ∧
      match xstep P x ρ c with
      | .inl c' => Encodes A.width fn (T ∪ (P.getD p.val (.base .reject)).touches c.mem) c'
          (Fin.castAddEmb A.extraTapes) o d' ∧
          ∃ q jump, d'.state = some q ∧
            A.redirect (some (p, par)) q = some (A.resumeTag p par jump) ∧
            c'.pc = if jump then jumpTarget (P.getD p.val (.base .reject)) else c.pc + 1
      | .inr v => d'.state = none ∧ d'.output = (if fn then c.out else [v]) := by
  let σ : Fin 8 ↪ Fin (8 + A.extraTapes) := Fin.castAddEmb A.extraTapes
  let R := A.phases p
  let bank := runBank σ R.entry d
  have hbank : Encodes A.width fn T c (Function.Embedding.refl _) o bank :=
    (runBank_encodes A.width fn T c σ o R.entry d).mp he
  obtain ⟨t, e, ht, hguard, henv, hrun, hpost⟩ :=
    R.correct b P ρ T c o bank hfetch hcoin (runBank_state σ R.entry d) hbank
  have hstart : embedEmitCfg σ d.workTapes d.workTapePos [] bank = d :=
    runBank_embed σ R.entry d hd
  have hr : ∀ u, ((A.phase (some (p, par))).fixChoice b).runFrom d u =
      embedEmitCfg σ d.workTapes d.workTapePos [] ((R.machine.fixChoice b).runFrom bank u) := by
    intro u
    rw [phase_some, runEmbedND_fixChoice]
    have h := embedEmitTM_runFrom σ (R.machine.fixChoice b) d.workTapes d.workTapePos [] bank u
    rwa [hstart] at h
  refine ⟨t, embedEmitCfg σ d.workTapes d.workTapePos [] e, ht, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro u hu q hq
    rw [hr u, embedEmitCfg_state] at hq
    rw [redirect_some, hguard u hu q hq, Option.map_none]
  · intro u hu j
    rw [hr u, embedEmitCfg_selected_pos]
    exact henv u hu j
  · intro u hu j hj
    rw [hr u]
    exact (embedEmitCfg_unselected σ _ _ _ _ j hj).2
  · rw [hr t, hrun]
  · cases hs : xstep P x ρ c with
    | inl c' =>
      rw [hs] at hpost
      obtain ⟨he', q, jump, hq, hred, hp⟩ := hpost
      refine ⟨(encodes_embed A.width fn _ c' σ o e d.workTapes d.workTapePos).mp he',
        q, jump, ?_, ?_, hp⟩
      · rw [embedEmitCfg_state]
        exact hq
      · rw [redirect_some, hred, Option.map_some]
    | inr v =>
      rw [hs] at hpost
      rw [embedEmitCfg_state, embedEmitCfg_output, List.nil_append]
      exact hpost

/-- An ambient instruction phase follows the fixed slice determined by its entry choice on
every prefix. Non-coin phases impose no condition on the branch's first bit.

**Proof sketch.** Reconstruct the ambient configuration from its selected entry bank. Transfer
the branch with `runEmbedND_runWith`, apply `RunPhase.branch_prefix_choice` on the eight source
tapes, and transfer the deterministic run back with `embedEmitTM_runFrom`. -/
theorem phase_branch_prefix (p : Fin (P.length + 1)) (par b : Bool) {x : List Bool}
    (d : Turing.Cfg (8 + A.extraTapes) Bool (A.PhaseState (some (p, par))) x)
    (hd : d.state = some (A.phases p).entry) (w : List Bool)
    (hb : isCoin (P.getD p.val (.base .reject)) = true → w ≠ [] → w.headD false = b)
    (u : ℕ) (hu : u ≤ w.length) :
    (A.phase (some (p, par))).runWith (w.take u) d =
      ((A.phase (some (p, par))).fixChoice b).runFrom d u := by
  let σ : Fin 8 ↪ Fin (8 + A.extraTapes) := Fin.castAddEmb A.extraTapes
  let R := A.phases p
  let bank := runBank σ R.entry d
  have hstart : embedEmitCfg σ d.workTapes d.workTapePos [] bank = d :=
    runBank_embed σ R.entry d hd
  have hleft := runEmbedND_runWith σ R.machine d.workTapes d.workTapePos [] (w.take u) bank
  have hright := embedEmitTM_runFrom σ (R.machine.fixChoice b) d.workTapes d.workTapePos [] bank u
  rw [hstart] at hleft hright
  rw [R.branch_prefix_choice b w bank hb u hu] at hleft
  rw [phase_some, runEmbedND_fixChoice]
  exact hleft.trans hright.symm

/-- If the fixed instruction slice reaches no redirect before the end of a choice word,
every host prefix is that slice with its state tagged by the instruction position/parity.

**Proof sketch.** At each prefix, `phase_branch_prefix` identifies the phase run with the
fixed slice. The slice's cut therefore supplies the guard for `host_phase_run`; nested takes
reduce to the original word's prefixes. This also works when the slice halts at its end. -/
theorem host_slice_prefix (p : Fin (P.length + 1)) (par b : Bool) {x : List Bool}
    (d : Turing.Cfg (8 + A.extraTapes) Bool (A.PhaseState (some (p, par))) x)
    (hd : d.state = some (A.phases p).entry) (w : List Bool)
    (hb : isCoin (P.getD p.val (.base .reject)) = true → w ≠ [] → w.headD false = b)
    (hcut : ∀ v < w.length, ∀ q,
      (((A.phase (some (p, par))).fixChoice b).runFrom d v).state = some q →
        A.redirect (some (p, par)) q = none) :
    ∀ u ≤ w.length, A.host.runWith (w.take u) (d.mapState (Sigma.mk (some (p, par)))) =
      (((A.phase (some (p, par))).fixChoice b).runFrom d u).mapState
        (Sigma.mk (some (p, par))) := by
  intro u hu
  have hguard : ∀ v < (w.take u).length, ∀ q,
      ((A.phase (some (p, par))).runWith ((w.take u).take v) d).state = some q →
        A.redirect (some (p, par)) q = none := by
    intro v hv q hq
    have hvu : v < u := by rw [List.length_take_of_le hu] at hv; exact hv
    rw [List.take_take, Nat.min_eq_left hvu.le,
      phase_branch_prefix A p par b d hd w hb v (hvu.le.trans hu)] at hq
    exact hcut v (hvu.trans_le hu) q hq
  rw [host_phase_run A (some (p, par)) d (w.take u) hguard,
    phase_branch_prefix A p par b d hd w hb u hu]

/-- **The local entry of a live host start.** A host configuration at the entry of the phase for
the instruction at `c.pc` is the local phase configuration at that entry, retagged; the local
configuration carries the same encoding. Shared by `host_ordinary` and `host_verdict`.

**Proof sketch.** Rename every state to the phase's entry: the state reader and `hd` give the
local entry, `encodes_mapState` transports the encoding, and `runEntry_reconstruct` retags it
back to `d`; renaming keeps the heads. -/
theorem host_local {x : List Bool} {W : ℕ} (par : Bool) (T : Finset ℤ) (c : XCfg W)
    (o : Fin 8 → ℤ) (d : Turing.Cfg (8 + A.extraTapes) Bool A.State x)
    (hd : d.state = some ⟨some (runPosition P c.pc, par),
      (A.phases (runPosition P c.pc)).entry⟩)
    (he : Encodes A.width fn T c (Fin.castAddEmb A.extraTapes) o d) :
    ∃ locald : Turing.Cfg (8 + A.extraTapes) Bool (A.phases (runPosition P c.pc)).State x,
      locald.state = some (A.phases (runPosition P c.pc)).entry ∧
      Encodes A.width fn T c (Fin.castAddEmb A.extraTapes) o locald ∧
      locald.mapState (Sigma.mk (some (runPosition P c.pc, par))) = d ∧
      locald.workTapePos = d.workTapePos := by
  let R := A.phases (runPosition P c.pc)
  refine ⟨d.mapState (fun _ => R.entry), ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [Cfg.mapState_state, hd]; rfl
  · exact (encodes_mapState A.width fn T c (Fin.castAddEmb A.extraTapes) o d
      (fun _ => R.entry)).mp he
  · exact runEntry_reconstruct R.entry
      (fun q : R.State => (⟨some (runPosition P c.pc, par), q⟩ : A.State)) d hd
  · funext j
    rw [Cfg.mapState_workTapePos]

/-- A word of each positive length headed by `b`: its nonempty values start with `b`. Shared
by `host_ordinary` and `host_verdict`. -/
theorem words_headD {b : Bool} (words : ℕ → List Bool) (hlen : ∀ n, (words n).length = n)
    (hhead : ∀ n, 0 < n → (words n).headD false = b) (t : ℕ) (hne : words t ≠ []) :
    (words t).headD false = b := by
  apply hhead t
  rw [← hlen t]
  exact List.length_pos_iff.mpr hne

/-- The ambient head envelope of a phase prefix started at the local entry: a selected tape stays
within the phase's envelope about its encoded origin, and an unselected tape is where the frame
clause leaves it. Shared by `host_ordinary` and `host_verdict`.

**Proof sketch.** Split on whether the tape is selected. A selected head of `d` sits at its
origin by the encoding, which the envelope bounds; an unselected one equals the local start,
whose heads are `d`'s. -/
theorem host_envelope {x : List Bool} {W : ℕ} {S : Type} (T : Finset ℤ) (c : XCfg W)
    (o : Fin 8 → ℤ) (d : Turing.Cfg (8 + A.extraTapes) Bool A.State x)
    (he : Encodes A.width fn T c (Fin.castAddEmb A.extraTapes) o d)
    (locald e : Turing.Cfg (8 + A.extraTapes) Bool S x)
    (hpos : locald.workTapePos = d.workTapePos) (B : ℕ)
    (henv : ∀ r : Fin 8, |e.workTapePos (Fin.castAddEmb A.extraTapes r) - o r| ≤ (B : ℤ))
    (hframe : ∀ j : Fin (8 + A.extraTapes), j ∉ Set.range (Fin.castAddEmb A.extraTapes) →
      e.workTapePos j = locald.workTapePos j)
    (j : Fin (8 + A.extraTapes)) :
    |e.workTapePos j - d.workTapePos j| ≤ (B : ℤ) := by
  by_cases hj : j ∈ Set.range (Fin.castAddEmb A.extraTapes)
  · obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := hj
    rw [((encodes_iff A.width fn T c (Fin.castAddEmb A.extraTapes) o d).mp he).1 r]
    exact henv r
  · rw [hframe j hj, hpos, sub_self, abs_zero]
    exact Nat.cast_nonneg _

/-- A continuing RAM instruction is simulated by one phase word and one dispatch choice.
The endpoint encodes its successor at the opposite parity, every head is restored, and every
prefix stays within the instruction's envelope around its starting heads.

**Proof sketch.** Retag the live host start to the local entry and apply `phase_correct`.
`phase_branch_prefix` transfers the supplied word to that fixed slice. The standard host
dispatch lemma supplies the tagged prefixes and the stationary final dispatch; `resumeTag_of_step`
identifies its destination with the successor RAM counter. The endpoint encoding fixes each
selected head at its original origin, while the frame clause fixes every extra head. These
same two cases bound each prefix, including the dispatch endpoint. -/
theorem host_ordinary {x ρ : List Bool} {W : ℕ} (par b : Bool)
    (T : Finset ℤ) (c c' : XCfg W) (o : Fin 8 → ℤ)
    (d : Turing.Cfg (8 + A.extraTapes) Bool A.State x)
    (hd : d.state = some ⟨some (runPosition P c.pc, par),
      (A.phases (runPosition P c.pc)).entry⟩)
    (he : Encodes A.width fn T c (Fin.castAddEmb A.extraTapes) o d)
    (hstep : xstep P x ρ c = .inl c')
    (hcoin : isCoin (P.getD c.pc (.base .reject)) = true → ρ.getD c.rd false = b)
    (words : ℕ → List Bool) (hlen : ∀ n, (words n).length = n)
    (hhead : ∀ n, 0 < n → (words n).headD false = b) (dispatch : ℕ → Bool) :
    ∃ (t : ℕ) (d' : Turing.Cfg (8 + A.extraTapes) Bool A.State x),
      t ≤ (A.phases (runPosition P c.pc)).cost *
        ((T.card + 1) * (W + 1) + W ^ 2 + x.length + 1) ∧
      A.host.runWith (words t ++ [dispatch t]) d = d' ∧
      d'.state = some ⟨some (runPosition P c'.pc, !par),
        (A.phases (runPosition P c'.pc)).entry⟩ ∧
      Encodes A.width fn (T ∪ (P.getD c.pc (.base .reject)).touches c.mem) c'
        (Fin.castAddEmb A.extraTapes) o d' ∧
      d'.workTapePos = d.workTapePos ∧
      ∀ u ≤ t + 1, ∀ j,
        |(A.host.runWith ((words t ++ [dispatch t]).take u) d).workTapePos j - d.workTapePos j| ≤
          ((A.phases (runPosition P c.pc)).cost *
            ((T.card + 1) * (W + 1) + (Nat.bits x.length).length + 1) : ℕ) := by
  let p := runPosition P c.pc
  let i : Index (P := P) := some (p, par)
  let σ : Fin 8 ↪ Fin (8 + A.extraTapes) := Fin.castAddEmb A.extraTapes
  let R := A.phases p
  have hfetch : P.getD p.val (.base .reject) = P.getD c.pc (.base .reject) :=
    runPosition_fetch P c.pc
  obtain ⟨locald, hd₀, he₀, hstart, hpos⟩ := A.host_local par T c o d hd he
  have hc : isCoin (P.getD p.val (.base .reject)) = true → ρ.getD c.rd false = b := by
    rw [hfetch]
    exact hcoin
  obtain ⟨t, e, ht, hcut, henv, hframe, hrun, hpost⟩ :=
    A.phase_correct p par b ρ T c o locald hfetch.symm hc hd₀ he₀
  rw [hstep] at hpost
  obtain ⟨he', q, jump, hq, hred, hpc⟩ := hpost
  let w := words t
  have hw : w.length = t := hlen t
  have hb : isCoin (P.getD p.val (.base .reject)) = true → w ≠ [] → w.headD false = b :=
    fun _ => words_headD words hlen hhead t
  have hrw := A.phase_branch_prefix p par b locald hd₀ w hb w.length le_rfl
  rw [List.take_length, hw, hrun] at hrw
  have hg : ∀ u < w.length, ∀ q,
      ((A.phase i).runWith (w.take u) locald).state = some q → A.redirect i q = none := by
    intro u hu q hqu
    rw [A.phase_branch_prefix p par b locald hd₀ w hb u hu.le] at hqu
    exact hcut u (by omega) q hqu
  obtain ⟨hpre, hfinal⟩ := A.host_phase_dispatch i locald e w hrw q hq
    (A.resumeTag p par jump) hred hg (dispatch t)
  rw [hstart] at hpre hfinal
  have hdest := A.resumeTag_of_step par jump hstep hpc
  let post := e.mapState (fun _ => A.resumeTag p par jump)
  have hheads : post.workTapePos = d.workTapePos := by
    funext j
    by_cases hj : j ∈ Set.range σ
    · obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := hj
      have heh := ((encodes_iff A.width fn _ c' σ o e).mp he').1 r
      have hdh := ((encodes_iff A.width fn T c σ o d).mp he).1 r
      rw [Cfg.mapState_workTapePos, heh, hdh]
    · have hf := hframe t le_rfl j hj
      rw [hrun] at hf
      rw [Cfg.mapState_workTapePos, hf, hpos]
  refine ⟨t, post, ht, hfinal, ?_, ?_, hheads, ?_⟩
  · rw [Cfg.mapState_state, hq, Option.map_some, hdest]
  · simpa only [hfetch] using
      (encodes_mapState A.width fn _ c' σ o e (fun _ => A.resumeTag p par jump)).mp he'
  · intro u hu j
    by_cases hut : u ≤ t
    · have huw : u ≤ w.length := by omega
      rw [List.take_append_of_le_length huw, hpre u huw,
        A.phase_branch_prefix p par b locald hd₀ w hb u huw, Cfg.mapState_workTapePos]
      exact A.host_envelope T c o d he locald _ hpos _ (henv u hut) (hframe u hut) j
    · have hue : u = t + 1 := by omega
      have hwle : (w ++ [dispatch t]).length ≤ u := by
        rw [List.length_append, hw, List.length_singleton, hue]
      rw [List.take_of_length_le hwle, hfinal, hheads, sub_self, abs_zero]
      exact Nat.cast_nonneg _

/-- A verdict instruction halts the host with the requested verdict/function output, with no
dispatch after it. Every prefix satisfies the same fixed-origin phase envelope.

**Proof sketch.** Apply `phase_correct` to the local entry after replacing the host tag.
A verdict is not a coin, so the entry-bit premise is vacuous. `host_slice_prefix` transfers
the entire word and all its prefixes; the final phase state is already halted. State and
output renaming equations preserve that endpoint, and the selected/frame cases give the
ambient head bound exactly as in the ordinary-step interface. -/
theorem host_verdict {x ρ : List Bool} {W : ℕ} (par b : Bool)
    (T : Finset ℤ) (c : XCfg W) (v : Bool) (o : Fin 8 → ℤ)
    (d : Turing.Cfg (8 + A.extraTapes) Bool A.State x)
    (hd : d.state = some ⟨some (runPosition P c.pc, par),
      (A.phases (runPosition P c.pc)).entry⟩)
    (he : Encodes A.width fn T c (Fin.castAddEmb A.extraTapes) o d)
    (hstep : xstep P x ρ c = .inr v)
    (words : ℕ → List Bool) (hlen : ∀ n, (words n).length = n)
    (hhead : ∀ n, 0 < n → (words n).headD false = b) :
    ∃ (t : ℕ) (d' : Turing.Cfg (8 + A.extraTapes) Bool A.State x),
      t ≤ (A.phases (runPosition P c.pc)).cost *
        ((T.card + 1) * (W + 1) + W ^ 2 + x.length + 1) ∧
      A.host.runWith (words t) d = d' ∧ d'.state = none ∧
      d'.output = (if fn then c.out else [v]) ∧
      ∀ u ≤ t, ∀ j,
        |(A.host.runWith ((words t).take u) d).workTapePos j - d.workTapePos j| ≤
          ((A.phases (runPosition P c.pc)).cost *
            ((T.card + 1) * (W + 1) + (Nat.bits x.length).length + 1) : ℕ) := by
  let p := runPosition P c.pc
  let i : Index (P := P) := some (p, par)
  let σ : Fin 8 ↪ Fin (8 + A.extraTapes) := Fin.castAddEmb A.extraTapes
  let R := A.phases p
  have hfetch : P.getD p.val (.base .reject) = P.getD c.pc (.base .reject) :=
    runPosition_fetch P c.pc
  obtain ⟨locald, hd₀, he₀, hstart, hpos⟩ := A.host_local par T c o d hd he
  have hc : isCoin (P.getD p.val (.base .reject)) = true → ρ.getD c.rd false = b := by
    intro h
    rw [hfetch, source_verdict_not_coin hstep] at h
    cases h
  obtain ⟨t, e, ht, hcut, henv, hframe, hrun, hpost⟩ :=
    A.phase_correct p par b ρ T c o locald hfetch.symm hc hd₀ he₀
  rw [hstep] at hpost
  let w := words t
  have hw : w.length = t := hlen t
  have hb : isCoin (P.getD p.val (.base .reject)) = true → w ≠ [] → w.headD false = b :=
    fun _ => words_headD words hlen hhead t
  have hc' : ∀ u < w.length, ∀ q,
      (((A.phase (some (p, par))).fixChoice b).runFrom locald u).state = some q →
        A.redirect (some (p, par)) q = none := by
    intro u hu q hq
    exact hcut u (by omega) q hq
  have hpre := A.host_slice_prefix p par b locald hd₀ w hb hc'
  rw [hstart] at hpre
  have hfinal := hpre w.length le_rfl
  rw [List.take_length, hw, hrun] at hfinal
  refine ⟨t, e.mapState (Sigma.mk i), ht, hfinal, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [Cfg.mapState_state, hpost.1, Option.map_none]
  · rw [Cfg.mapState_output]
    exact hpost.2
  · intro u hu j
    have huw : u ≤ w.length := by omega
    rw [hpre u huw, Cfg.mapState_workTapePos]
    exact A.host_envelope T c o d he locald _ hpos _ (henv u hu) (hframe u hu) j

end WordRAM.Sim.RunSetup
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/RAMSimulation/Sim/Encoding.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 Seyoon Ragavan. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Programs.WordRAM.Extended
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.KeyTable

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Stage 2's simulation: how tapes encode a configuration of the extended word RAM

The simulating machine of `WordRAM.exists_simulation` keeps a configuration `c : XCfg W` of the
extended word RAM on eight work tapes, its program position in its finite control. This file
defines that encoding, `WordRAM.Sim.Encodes`, shared by the start-up (`Sim/Startup`), the
instruction phases (`Sim/Phases`) and the simulation's induction. The declarations of the
`WordRAM.Sim` namespace are the simulation's internal interfaces: public so that the pieces can
live in separate files, not meant for other consumers.

**The eight tapes.**
* `0`: the memory, a keyed table (`Turing.KeyTableAt`) of the written cells and their words.
* `1`: the key register, `W + a` cells.
* `2`, `3`, `4`: three word registers of `W` cells.
* `5`: the input length in binary, `Nat.bits |x|`.
* `6`, `7`: blank scratch tapes.

**Keys.** The memory is indexed by integers. A cell `z` is stored under the `W + a` bits of
`z` in two's complement, `keyBits a W z`. Every address the program touches is in that range:
a computed address is a word's signed value, and the program's own addresses (its immediates)
are below `2^(a-1)` in absolute value (`WordRAM.Sim.ImmBound`). In that range distinct cells
have distinct keys.

## Main definitions

* `WordRAM.Sim.keyBits`, `WordRAM.Sim.immediates`, `WordRAM.Sim.ImmBound`.
* `WordRAM.Sim.TableOf`: a list of entries stores a memory over a set of cells.
* `WordRAM.Sim.Encodes`: the tapes encode a configuration.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (Exercise 1.9.)
* [AFM26] Anthropic, PBC, `anthropics/formal-math`, project `3sum-apsp`, commit `e1a4e650`,
  Apache-2.0: the word RAM (`TCSlib/Programs/WordRAM/Basic.lean`), extended in
  `TCSlib/Programs/WordRAM/Extended.lean`.
-/

namespace WordRAM.Sim

open Turing

/-- **The key of a cell**: the `W + a` bits of the integer `z` in two's complement, least
significant first. -/
def keyBits (a W : ℕ) (z : ℤ) : List Bool := bvBits (BitVec.ofInt (W + a) z)

/-- The key of a cell, as an equation. -/
theorem keyBits_def (a W : ℕ) (z : ℤ) : keyBits a W z = bvBits (BitVec.ofInt (W + a) z) := rfl

/-- **The addresses written in an instruction**: its integer arguments, which name cells (the
label of `bltz` is a position, not a cell, and is not one of them). -/
def immediates : XInstr → List ℤ
  | .base (.one i) => [i]
  | .base (.add i j k) => [i, j, k]
  | .base (.sub i j k) => [i, j, k]
  | .base (.mul i j k) => [i, j, k]
  | .base (.load i j) => [i, j]
  | .base (.store i j) => [i, j]
  | .base (.bltz i _) => [i]
  | .base .accept => []
  | .base .reject => []
  | .rdIn i j => [i, j]
  | .emit i => [i]
  | .coin i => [i]
  | .half i j => [i, j]

/-- The addresses written in an instruction, as an equation. -/
theorem immediates_def (ins : XInstr) :
    immediates ins =
      match ins with
      | .base (.one i) => [i]
      | .base (.add i j k) => [i, j, k]
      | .base (.sub i j k) => [i, j, k]
      | .base (.mul i j k) => [i, j, k]
      | .base (.load i j) => [i, j]
      | .base (.store i j) => [i, j]
      | .base (.bltz i _) => [i]
      | .base .accept => []
      | .base .reject => []
      | .rdIn i j => [i, j]
      | .emit i => [i]
      | .coin i => [i]
      | .half i j => [i, j] := by
  rcases ins with ins | _ | _ | _ | _ <;> try rfl

/-- **Small immediates**: every address written in `ins` is in the signed range of `a` bits
(`WordRAM.InRange a`), so that it has a key of `W + a` bits for every `W`. -/
def ImmBound (a : ℕ) (ins : XInstr) : Prop := ∀ z ∈ immediates ins, InRange a z

/-- `ImmBound`, as an equivalence with its definition. -/
theorem immBound_iff (a : ℕ) (ins : XInstr) :
    ImmBound a ins ↔ ∀ z ∈ immediates ins, InRange a z := Iff.rfl

/-- **A table stores a memory over a set of cells.** `TableOf a W T m es`: the keys of `es` are
distinct; every entry is the key of some cell `z ∈ T` in the range of `W + a` bits, with `m z`'s
bits as its value; and every cell in that range where `m` is nonzero has an entry. So a lookup of
a cell in range finds its word when it has an entry, and finds nothing only when the word is `0`
(an entry may still hold the word `0`); and `es` has at most `|T|` entries. -/
def TableOf (a W : ℕ) (T : Finset ℤ) (m : ℤ → BitVec W) (es : List (List Bool × List Bool)) :
    Prop :=
  (es.map Prod.fst).Nodup ∧
    (∀ e ∈ es, ∃ z ∈ T, InRange (W + a) z ∧ e = (keyBits a W z, bvBits (m z))) ∧
    ∀ z : ℤ, InRange (W + a) z → m z ≠ 0 → keyBits a W z ∈ es.map Prod.fst

/-- `TableOf`, as an equivalence with its definition. -/
theorem tableOf_iff (a W : ℕ) (T : Finset ℤ) (m : ℤ → BitVec W)
    (es : List (List Bool × List Bool)) :
    TableOf a W T m es ↔ (es.map Prod.fst).Nodup ∧
      (∀ e ∈ es, ∃ z ∈ T, InRange (W + a) z ∧ e = (keyBits a W z, bvBits (m z))) ∧
      ∀ z : ℤ, InRange (W + a) z → m z ≠ 0 → keyBits a W z ∈ es.map Prod.fst :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- **The tapes encode a configuration.** `Encodes a fn T c σ o d`, for the eight tapes placed in
`d`'s tapes by `σ`, with origins `o`:
* every one of the eight heads is at its origin;
* tape `0` holds a keyed table that stores `c.mem` over the cells `T` (`TableOf`);
* tape `1` holds a word of `W + a` cells, tapes `2` to `4` words of `W` cells;
* tape `5` holds `Nat.bits |x|`;
* tapes `6` and `7` are blank;
* the output is `c.out` in function mode (`fn = true`) and empty in verdict mode.

The program position `c.pc` and the coin count `c.rd` are not on the tapes: the position is the
phase of the machine's finite control, and the coin count is a property of the run. -/
def Encodes {K : ℕ} {S : Type} (a : ℕ) (fn : Bool) {x : List Bool} {W : ℕ} (T : Finset ℤ)
    (c : XCfg W) (σ : Fin 8 ↪ Fin K) (o : Fin 8 → ℤ) (d : Turing.Cfg K Bool S x) : Prop :=
  (∀ j : Fin 8, d.workTapePos (σ j) = o j) ∧
    (∃ es, KeyTableAt d (σ 0) (o 0) es ∧ TableOf a W T c.mem es) ∧
    (∃ w, WordAt d (σ 1) w ∧ w.length = W + a) ∧
    (∀ r : Fin 8, 2 ≤ r.val → r.val ≤ 4 → ∃ w, WordAt d (σ r) w ∧ w.length = W) ∧
    WordAt d (σ 5) (Nat.bits x.length) ∧
    (∀ r : Fin 8, 6 ≤ r.val → ∀ q : ℤ, d.workTapes (σ r) q = none) ∧
    d.output = if fn then c.out else []

/-- `Encodes`, as an equivalence with its definition. -/
theorem encodes_iff {K : ℕ} {S : Type} (a : ℕ) (fn : Bool) {x : List Bool} {W : ℕ}
    (T : Finset ℤ) (c : XCfg W) (σ : Fin 8 ↪ Fin K) (o : Fin 8 → ℤ) (d : Turing.Cfg K Bool S x) :
    Encodes a fn T c σ o d ↔
      (∀ j : Fin 8, d.workTapePos (σ j) = o j) ∧
      (∃ es, KeyTableAt d (σ 0) (o 0) es ∧ TableOf a W T c.mem es) ∧
      (∃ w, WordAt d (σ 1) w ∧ w.length = W + a) ∧
      (∀ r : Fin 8, 2 ≤ r.val → r.val ≤ 4 → ∃ w, WordAt d (σ r) w ∧ w.length = W) ∧
      WordAt d (σ 5) (Nat.bits x.length) ∧
      (∀ r : Fin 8, 6 ≤ r.val → ∀ q : ℤ, d.workTapes (σ r) q = none) ∧
      d.output = if fn then c.out else [] :=
  Iff.rfl

end WordRAM.Sim
```

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 Seyoon Ragavan. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.RAMSimulation.Sim.Encoding
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Embed
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.InputLength
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Contract
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.InterpreterStartup
import TCSlib.Complexity.RAMSimulation.WordSize

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

attribute [local irreducible] Turing.Contract.ofReaches

/-!
# Stage 2's simulation: the start-up

Before the first instruction, the simulating machine computes the word size `W = W (|x|)` with
the word-size witness, prepares its eight tapes and installs the start memory: the cell `-1`
holds `|x|` modulo `2^W` and every other cell `0` (`WordRAM.initMem`). This file constructs that
start-up for any word-size witness `Mw`; its extra tapes hold `Mw`'s tapes, and its output, which
is captured on a work tape.

## Main results

* `WordRAM.Sim.exists_startup`: the start-up reaches a configuration encoding
  `XCfg.init W |x|` within `tw + O(|x| + W² + 1)` steps and `sw + O(W + log |x| + 1)` cells,
  where `Mw` writes `Nat.bits W` within `tw` steps and `sw` cells.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (Exercise 1.9; §4.1, space-constructible functions.)
-/

namespace WordRAM.Sim

open Turing

/-! ## Private facts about the initial memory -/

/-- The marked startup entry stores the length word at the distinguished cell. -/
private theorem startup_initMem_neg_one (W n : ℕ) : initMem W n (-1) = wd W n := by
  rw [initMem_def, Function.update_self]

/-- Every other startup cell holds zero. -/
private theorem startup_initMem_of_ne (W n : ℕ) (z : ℤ) (hz : z ≠ -1) :
    initMem W n z = 0 := by
  rw [initMem_def, Function.update_of_ne hz]

/-- The singleton table is the initial memory as soon as the distinguished cell's signed
range obligation is supplied. This isolates that obligation from the tape construction.

**Proof sketch.** Use `tableOf_iff`. The singleton has distinct keys and its entry is the key
of `-1`, with the word given by `initMem_def`. For completeness, a nonzero cell must equal
`-1`, since `initMem_def` makes every other cell zero. -/
private theorem startup_tableOf (a W n : ℕ) (hr : InRange (W + a) (-1)) :
    TableOf a W {-1} (initMem W n) [(keyBits a W (-1), bvBits (wd W n))] := by
  rw [tableOf_iff]
  refine ⟨by simp only [List.map_cons, List.map_nil, List.nodup_cons, List.not_mem_nil,
      not_false_eq_true, List.nodup_nil, and_self], ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro e he
    simp only [List.mem_singleton] at he
    subst e
    refine ⟨-1, Finset.mem_singleton_self _, hr, ?_⟩
    rw [startup_initMem_neg_one]
  · intro z _ hz
    have he : z = -1 := by
      by_contra hne
      exact hz (startup_initMem_of_ne W n z hne)
    subst z
    simp only [List.map_cons, List.map_nil, List.mem_singleton]

/-- Every positive width represents `-1`, including the single-bit boundary. -/
private theorem startup_inRange_neg_one (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) : InRange k (-1) := by
  rw [inRange_iff]
  have hp : (2 : ℤ) ^ 1 ≤ 2 ^ k := pow_le_pow_right₀ (by norm_num) hk
  norm_num at hp ⊢
  constructor <;> omega

/-- Every width at least two represents `-1` in the signed range. -/
private theorem startup_inRange_neg_one_of_two_le (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) : InRange k (-1) := by
  exact startup_inRange_neg_one k (by omega)

/-- The finished eight tapes encode the initial RAM configuration once the distinguished
address's range fact is supplied.

**Proof sketch.** Read the encoding with `encodes_iff` and initialization with `XCfg.init_def`.
The table clause is `startup_tableOf`; the register, length, scratch and origin clauses are the
hypotheses. The initial output is empty in either output mode. -/
private theorem startup_encodes_of_tapes {K : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool} {W : ℕ}
    (a : ℕ) (fn : Bool) (σ : Fin 8 ↪ Fin K) (o : Fin 8 → ℤ) (d : Turing.Cfg K Bool S x)
    (hr : InRange (W + a) (-1))
    (hheads : ∀ j : Fin 8, d.workTapePos (σ j) = o j)
    (htable : KeyTableAt d (σ 0) (o 0)
      [(keyBits a W (-1), bvBits (wd W x.length))])
    (hkey : ∃ w, WordAt d (σ 1) w ∧ w.length = W + a)
    (hregs : ∀ r : Fin 8, 2 ≤ r.val → r.val ≤ 4 → ∃ w, WordAt d (σ r) w ∧ w.length = W)
    (hlen : WordAt d (σ 5) (Nat.bits x.length))
    (hblank : ∀ r : Fin 8, 6 ≤ r.val → ∀ q : ℤ, d.workTapes (σ r) q = none)
    (hout : d.output = []) : Encodes a fn {-1} (XCfg.init W x.length) σ o d := by
  rw [encodes_iff, XCfg.init_def]
  refine ⟨hheads, ⟨_, htable, startup_tableOf a W x.length hr⟩, hkey, hregs, hlen, hblank, ?_⟩
  cases fn <;> simpa only [Bool.false_eq_true, if_false, if_true] using hout

/-! ## Private word and capture facts -/

/-- The length word consists of the low input-length bits, padded by false bits to its width. -/
private theorem startup_lengthWord (W n : ℕ) :
    bvBits (wd W n) = List.ofFn (fun j : Fin W => (Nat.bits n).getD j.val false) := by
  change bvBits (BitVec.ofInt W (n : ℤ)) = _
  rw [BitVec.ofInt_natCast, bvBits_def]
  apply congrArg (fun f : Fin W → Bool => List.ofFn f)
  funext j
  rw [BitVec.getLsbD_ofNat]
  simp only [j.isLt, decide_true, Bool.true_and]
  rw [Nat.testBit_eq_inth, ← List.getD_default_eq_getI]
  rfl

/-- The shared returning silent embedding captures the width witness at its first live exit.

**Proof sketch.** Read the bounded computation with `FinTM.computesInTime_iff`, invoke
`embedSilentRetTM_firstReturn`, and identify the fresh start with `embedSilentCfg_initCfg`.
The capture and unselected-frame field readers give the binary width, its ending head,
the empty physical output and every untouched tape. -/
private theorem startup_capture {K : ℕ} (Mw : FinTM Bool) (σ : Fin Mw.k ↪ Fin K)
    (cap : Fin K) (hcap : cap ∉ Set.range σ) (x : List Bool) (W tw : ℕ)
    (hMw : Mw.ComputesInTime x (Nat.bits W) tw) :
    ∃ t ≤ tw,
      (∀ s < t, ((embedSilentRetTM σ cap Mw.tm).runFrom
        (Turing.Cfg.init (Sum.inl Mw.tm.q₀) x) s).state ≠ some (Sum.inr ())) ∧
      let d := (embedSilentRetTM σ cap Mw.tm).runFrom
        (Turing.Cfg.init (Sum.inl Mw.tm.q₀) x) t
      d.state = some (Sum.inr ()) ∧ d.workTapes cap = FinTM.bufferTape (Nat.bits W) ∧
        d.workTapePos cap = ((Nat.bits W).length : ℤ) ∧ d.output = [] ∧
        ∀ j, j ∉ Set.range σ → j ≠ cap →
          d.workTapes j = (fun _ => none) ∧ d.workTapePos j = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨halt, out⟩ := (FinTM.computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mp hMw
  obtain ⟨t, ht, run, cut⟩ := embedSilentRetTM_firstReturn Mw x σ cap hcap
    (fun _ _ => none) (fun _ => 0) [] tw halt
  rw [embedSilentCfg_initCfg Mw.tm σ cap hcap x] at run cut
  refine ⟨t, ht, cut, ?_⟩
  dsimp only
  rw [run]
  obtain ⟨word, head⟩ := embedSilentCfg_cap σ cap hcap (fun _ _ => none) (fun _ => 0)
    [] [] (Mw.tm.runFrom (Mw.tm.initCfg x) tw)
  rw [List.nil_append, out] at word head
  refine ⟨rfl, word, head, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [embedSilentCfg_output]
  · intro j hj hne
    exact embedSilentCfg_unselected σ cap (fun _ _ => none) (fun _ => 0)
      [] [] (Mw.tm.runFrom (Mw.tm.initCfg x) tw) j hj hne

/-- Place the width witness after the eight simulation tapes, before the auxiliary bank. -/
private def startupBank (m r : ℕ) : Fin m ↪ Fin (8 + (m + (r + 1))) :=
  (Fin.castAddEmb (r + 1)).trans (Fin.natAddEmb 8)

/-- The capture tape is the first tape of the final auxiliary bank. -/
private def startupCaptureIndex (m r : ℕ) : Fin (8 + (m + (r + 1))) :=
  Fin.natAdd 8 (Fin.natAdd m (0 : Fin (r + 1)))

/-- The auxiliary capture tape is disjoint from the width witness's bank. -/
private theorem startupCapture_separated (m r : ℕ) :
    startupCaptureIndex m r ∉ Set.range (startupBank m r) := by
  rintro ⟨j, hj⟩
  have h := congrArg Fin.val hj
  change 8 + j.val = 8 + (m + 0) at h
  have hj := j.isLt
  omega

/-- Silent capture adds only the frame/capture tapes' space, with coefficient one on the
width witness's original space.

**Proof sketch.** Rewrite returning visited sets with
`embedSilentRetTM_visitedByTapeHead`. On the selected bank they equal the source visited sets;
off it, the frame uses one cell and the capture uses at most the final output length plus one.
Split the actual tape sum twice with `Fin.sum_univ_add`, separating the first eight tapes,
the source bank, and the final auxiliary bank. The source sum is counted exactly once; bound
each remaining tape by the binary width's length plus one. -/
private theorem startup_capture_space (Mw : FinTM Bool) (r : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (W tw : ℕ)
    (hMw : Mw.ComputesInTime x (Nat.bits W) tw) :
    (embedSilentRetTM (startupBank Mw.k r) (startupCaptureIndex Mw.k r) Mw.tm).spaceUsed
      (Turing.Cfg.init (Sum.inl Mw.tm.q₀) x) tw ≤
      Mw.tm.spaceUsed (Mw.tm.initCfg x) tw + (8 + (r + 1)) * ((Nat.bits W).length + 1) := by
  classical
  let σ := startupBank Mw.k r
  let cap := startupCaptureIndex Mw.k r
  have hcap : cap ∉ Set.range σ := startupCapture_separated _ _
  let R := embedSilentRetTM σ cap Mw.tm
  let f := fun j => R.spaceUsedByTape (Turing.Cfg.init (Sum.inl Mw.tm.q₀) x) tw j
  have fresh := embedSilentCfg_initCfg Mw.tm σ cap hcap x
  have out := ((FinTM.computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mp hMw).2
  have selected (j : Fin Mw.k) : f (σ j) = Mw.tm.spaceUsedByTape (Mw.tm.initCfg x) tw j := by
    simp only [f, R]
    rw [← fresh, MultiTapeTM.spaceUsedByTape_eq_card, embedSilentRetTM_visitedByTapeHead,
      (embedSilentTM_visitedByTapeHead σ cap hcap Mw.tm (fun _ _ => none)
        (fun _ => 0) [] [] (Mw.tm.initCfg x) tw j).1,
      ← MultiTapeTM.spaceUsedByTape_eq_card]
  have frame (j) (hj : j ∉ Set.range σ) : f j ≤ (Nat.bits W).length + 1 := by
    simp only [f, R]
    rw [← fresh, MultiTapeTM.spaceUsedByTape_eq_card, embedSilentRetTM_visitedByTapeHead,
      ← MultiTapeTM.spaceUsedByTape_eq_card]
    by_cases he : j = cap
    · subst j
      have h := embedSilentTM_spaceUsedByTape_cap σ cap hcap Mw.tm (fun _ _ => none)
        (fun _ => 0) [] [] (Mw.tm.initCfg x) tw
      have hi : (Mw.tm.initCfg x).output = [] := by rw [MultiTapeTM.initCfg_eq, Cfg.init_output]
      rw [out, hi] at h
      simpa only [List.length_nil, Nat.sub_zero] using h
    · rw [(embedSilentTM_visitedByTapeHead_frame σ cap hcap Mw.tm (fun _ _ => none)
        (fun _ => 0) [] [] (Mw.tm.initCfg x) tw j hj he).2]
      omega
  have first : (∑ j : Fin 8, f (Fin.castAdd (Mw.k + (r + 1)) j)) ≤
      8 * ((Nat.bits W).length + 1) := by
    calc
      _ ≤ ∑ _j : Fin 8, ((Nat.bits W).length + 1) := by
        apply Finset.sum_le_sum
        intro j _
        apply frame
        rintro ⟨a, ha⟩
        have he := congrArg Fin.val ha
        change 8 + a.val = j.val at he
        have hj := j.isLt
        omega
      _ = _ := by simp
  have last : (∑ j : Fin (r + 1), f (Fin.natAdd 8 (Fin.natAdd Mw.k j))) ≤
      (r + 1) * ((Nat.bits W).length + 1) := by
    calc
      _ ≤ ∑ _j : Fin (r + 1), ((Nat.bits W).length + 1) := by
        apply Finset.sum_le_sum
        intro j _
        apply frame
        rintro ⟨a, ha⟩
        have he := congrArg Fin.val ha
        change 8 + a.val = 8 + (Mw.k + j.val) at he
        have ha := a.isLt
        omega
      _ = _ := by simp
  have middle : (∑ j : Fin Mw.k, f (Fin.natAdd 8 (Fin.castAdd (r + 1) j))) =
      Mw.tm.spaceUsed (Mw.tm.initCfg x) tw := by
    rw [MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed_eq_sum]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun j _ => selected j)
  rw [MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed_eq_sum]
  change (∑ j : Fin (8 + (Mw.k + (r + 1))), f j) ≤ _
  rw [Fin.sum_univ_add, Fin.sum_univ_add
    (fun j : Fin (Mw.k + (r + 1)) => f (Fin.natAdd 8 j)), middle, Nat.add_mul]
  omega

/-! ## Private expansion row -/

/-- The catalog expansion writes a zero register on tape zero and exhausts the binary
counter on tape one, returning only the counter head. -/
private def startupExpandPost {x : List Bool} {S : Type} (exit : S) (W : ℕ)
    (d : Turing.Cfg 2 Bool S x) : Turing.Cfg 2 Bool S x :=
  { d with
    state := some exit
    workTapes := Function.update
      (Function.update d.workTapes 0
        (wordPatch (d.workTapes 0) (d.workTapePos 0) (List.replicate W false))) 1
      (fun q => if d.workTapePos 1 ≤ q ∧
          q < d.workTapePos 1 + ((Nat.bits W).length : ℤ) then some true else d.workTapes 1 q)
    workTapePos := Function.update d.workTapePos 0 (d.workTapePos 0 + (W : ℤ)) }

/-- The existing counter-driven expansion supplies the zero-register writer at every width.

**Proof sketch.** Apply `expandTM_run_ofCfg` to `counterLoopBody 0 d` and the binary width on
the last tape. `counterLoopCfg_body` identifies its start. For the endpoint, compare the body
with the body of `startupExpandPost` through the published body-field readers and
`wordPatch_apply`; the same reconstruction theorem then identifies the entire host endpoint.
The catalog's cut excludes both loop exits, hence the desired `done` exit. -/
private theorem startup_expand_run {x : List Bool} (W : ℕ)
    (d : Turing.Cfg 2 Bool (CounterLoopState (Fin 2)) x)
    (hd : d.state = some (.dec .run)) (hw : WordAt d 1 (Nat.bits W)) :
    (expandTM 1 0 [false]).runFrom d (2 * W + counterOverhead (Nat.bits W) (W + 1)) =
      startupExpandPost .done W d ∧
    (∀ t < 2 * W + counterOverhead (Nat.bits W) (W + 1),
      ((expandTM 1 0 [false]).runFrom d t).state ≠ some .done) := by
  let c := counterLoopBody (0 : Fin 2) d
  let body : Turing.Cfg 1 Bool (Fin 2) x :=
    { c with
      workTapes := fun j q =>
        if j = 0 ∧ c.workTapePos j ≤ q ∧ q < c.workTapePos j + (W : ℤ) then
          FinTM.bufferTape (List.replicate W false) (q - c.workTapePos j)
        else c.workTapes j q
      workTapePos := Function.update c.workTapePos 0 (c.workTapePos 0 + (W : ℤ)) }
  have zero_cast : (0 : Fin 1).castSucc = (0 : Fin 2) := rfl
  have hb : body = counterLoopBody (0 : Fin 2) (startupExpandPost .done W d) := by
    apply Turing.Cfg.ext
    · simp only [body, c, counterLoopBody_state]
    · simp only [body, c, startupExpandPost, counterLoopBody_inputPos]
    · funext j q
      obtain rfl : j = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
      simp only [body, c, startupExpandPost, counterLoopBody_workTapes,
        counterLoopBody_workTapePos, zero_cast, Function.update_self,
        Function.update_of_ne (by decide : (0 : Fin 2) ≠ 1), wordPatch_apply, true_and,
        List.length_replicate]
    · funext j
      obtain rfl : j = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
      simp only [body, c, startupExpandPost, counterLoopBody_workTapePos, zero_cast,
        Function.update_self]
      change d.workTapePos 0 + (W : ℤ) =
        Function.update d.workTapePos 0 (d.workTapePos 0 + (W : ℤ)) (0 : Fin 2)
      rw [Function.update_self]
    · simp only [body, c, startupExpandPost, counterLoopBody_output]
  have hw' : ∀ q : ℤ, -1 ≤ q → q ≤ ((Nat.bits W).length : ℤ) →
      d.workTapes 1 (d.workTapePos 1 + q) = FinTM.bufferTape (Nat.bits W) q :=
    (wordAt_iff _ _ _).mp hw
  have value : Nat.ofDigits 2 ((Nat.bits W).map Bool.toNat) = W :=
    (counterValue_eq _).symm.trans (counterValue_bits W)
  obtain ⟨run, cut, -, -⟩ := expandTM_run_ofCfg (0 : Fin 1) [false] c
    (by rw [counterLoopBody_state]) (Nat.bits W) (d.workTapes 1) (d.workTapePos 1) hw' W value
  simp only [List.length_cons, List.length_nil, Nat.zero_add, Nat.mul_one,
    List.flatten_replicate_singleton, show (1 : ℕ) + 1 = 2 from rfl,
    Nat.mul_comm W 2] at run cut
  have start : counterLoopCfg (some (.dec .run)) c (d.workTapes 1) (d.workTapePos 1) = d := by
    rw [← hd]
    exact counterLoopCfg_body (0 : Fin 2) d
  rw [start] at run cut
  have finish : counterLoopCfg (some .done) body
      (fun q => if d.workTapePos 1 ≤ q ∧ q < d.workTapePos 1 + ((Nat.bits W).length : ℤ)
        then some true else d.workTapes 1 q) (d.workTapePos 1) = startupExpandPost .done W d := by
    rw [hb]
    exact counterLoopCfg_body (0 : Fin 2) (startupExpandPost .done W d)
  refine ⟨?_, fun t ht => (cut t ht).1⟩
  simpa only [body, Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one, Nat.cast_zero, Fin.val_zero, c,
    mul_comm 2 W] using run.trans finish

/-- Amortized counter overhead makes the zero-register expansion linear in the width. -/
private theorem startup_expand_time (W : ℕ) :
    2 * W + counterOverhead (Nat.bits W) (W + 1) ≤ 8 * W + 2 := by
  have h := counterOverhead_le (Nat.bits W)
  rw [(counterValue_eq _).symm.trans (counterValue_bits W)] at h
  have hlen := length_bits_le_self W
  omega

/-! ## Private composition of startup stages -/

/-- Erase only a configuration's finite control tag. -/
private def startupErase {K : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool}
    (d : Turing.Cfg K Bool S x) : Turing.Cfg K Bool Unit x := d.mapState (fun _ => ())

/-- Normalize erasure to physical fields before forming arithmetic-dependent conditionals. -/
private theorem startupErase_eq {K : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool}
    (d : Turing.Cfg K Bool S x) : startupErase d =
      ⟨d.state.map (fun _ => ()), d.inputPos, d.workTapes, d.workTapePos, d.output⟩ := by
  apply Turing.Cfg.ext <;> (try funext j) <;> (try funext q) <;>
```
